# SmallDivisorPulse — every small number divides a speed of any counterexample

**Generated file — do not edit.** Regenerated by `python scripts/graph.py`.

**Status:** proved in Lean · **Diagram:** [The Lonely Runner: pile-ups, shifts and residue sieves](../../GRAPH.md#the-lonely-runner-pile-ups-shifts-and-residue-sieves)

Normalize so the runner to be lonely stands still and the others have whole-number speeds. If no speed is divisible by some number from 2 up to the field size, then at the time one over that number every moving runner is at least one over that number from the start, which is enough. So in any set of speeds that is never lonely, every number from 2 up to the field size divides some speed, and their least common multiple divides the product of the speeds. Rosenfeld 2025, Lemma 4. The general form of the even/odd pulse. Uses only the vocabulary of PileUpLock (no claim of it), so no arrow is drawn. Times are fractions, as in PileUpLock.

## Claims

<a id="small_divisor_time_works"></a>
### `small_divisor_time_works`

If a number from 2 up to the number of runners divides none of the speeds, the time one over that number is lonely for the runner standing still.

```lean
/-- **One over a small number works when it divides no speed.** If `j` is from
2 up to the number of runners and divides none of the speeds, the time `1 / j`
is lonely for the runner standing still. -/
def small_divisor_time_works : Prop :=
  ∀ (S : Finset ℤ) (j : ℕ), 2 ≤ j → j ≤ S.card + 1 → (∀ v ∈ S, ¬ (j : ℤ) ∣ v) →
    lonely_at S j 1
```

**Rests on:** no other node (Mathlib and the Vocabulary only)

**Proof:** `RNS.SmallDivisorPulse.small_divisor_time_works_holds` in [`RNSSolutions/SmallDivisorPulse.lean`](../../RNSSolutions/SmallDivisorPulse.lean)

<a id="counterexample_lcm_dvd_product"></a>
### `counterexample_lcm_dvd_product`

If the runner standing still is never lonely, the least common multiple of 2 up to the number of runners divides the product of the speeds.

```lean
/-- **The small numbers divide the product of a counterexample's speeds.** If
the runner standing still never has a lonely moment, the least common multiple
of 2 up to the number of runners divides the product of the speeds. -/
def counterexample_lcm_dvd_product : Prop :=
  ∀ S : Finset ℤ, ¬ has_lonely_time S →
    (Finset.Icc 2 (S.card + 1)).lcm (fun j : ℕ => (j : ℤ)) ∣ ∏ v ∈ S, v
```

**Rests on:** [`SmallDivisorPulse.small_divisor_time_works`](SmallDivisorPulse.md#small_divisor_time_works)

**Proof:** `RNS.SmallDivisorPulse.counterexample_lcm_dvd_product_step` in [`RNSSolutions/SmallDivisorPulse.lean`](../../RNSSolutions/SmallDivisorPulse.lean)
